prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name a single “best” broker without knowing your specific needs (location, budget, whether it’s just you or you have employees, whether you want ACA marketplace plans or alternatives). If you tell me your ZIP code and whether you need an individual/family plan or a small-group/employer plan, I’ll pull a short list of well-rated local brokers who specialize in self-employed people.

Meanwhile, here’s a practical plan and what to look for so you can find the best broker for you:

Key questions I need (or you should consider)
- ZIP code (Kansas City, MO vs Kansas City, KS matters for networks and marketplace)
- Individual/family or small-group (do you have employees?)
- Age(s), general health needs (prescriptions, chronic conditions), preferred doctors/hospitals
- Monthly budget and whether you want lower premium vs lower out-of-pocket
- Do you want ACA/Marketplace plans (with potential subsidies) or are you open to short-term/association plans?
- Want in-person help or OK with phone/virtual?

How to find the best broker for a self-employed person
1. Prefer an independent broker or “navigator”
   - Independent brokers can quote multiple carriers and compare ACA plans. Marketplace navigators can help enroll in subsidized plans at no charge.
2. Verify credentials
   - Confirm they’re licensed in Missouri (or Kansas if applicable). Ask for their NPN (National Producer Number) and check with the Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance website.
3. Ask about fees and compensation
   - Some brokers are paid by insurers (no client fee); some may charge an enrollment or advisory fee. Get this up front.
4. Confirm marketplace experience
   - If you need ACA plans and subsidies, ensure they’re experienced enrolling clients through HealthCare.gov (or the Missouri exchange) and can estimate subsidies.
5. Check reviews and references
   - Look at Google/Yelp reviews, BBB, and ask the broker for local references of self-employed clients.
6. Ask the right questions
   - Which carriers and networks do you represent?
   - Will you compare ACA plans and off-marketplace alternatives?
   - How quickly can you get quotes and enrollment done?
   - How will you support me during annual renewal or if I have a claims issue?

Where to look right now
- HealthCare.gov (for ACA marketplace enrollment and finding local navigators)
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance (verify license status)
- Google/Yelp for “independent health insurance broker Kansas City MO” and check ratings
- Local community navigator organizations (often free help with marketplace enrollment)

If you want, I can:
- Look up 3–5 well-reviewed independent brokers or navigator organizations in your exact ZIP code
- Compare a couple of plan options (if you give age, household size, and income range)
Tell me your ZIP code and a bit about what you need and I’ll find tailored local recommendations.
